chapter: Kirby again, Garland gigs and later recordings
title: Garland band personnel and drummer Rick Harewood
summary: The band had trumpeter Sleepy, Bernhardt, third altos and a drummer Holmes recommended, Rick Harewood.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Well, now at times you had two trumpets. Who would carry the load, then? The other trumpeter?
Sleepy. That's all I know his name, Sleepy. Big, fat guy. I think he used to be with Jimmy Lunceford. I'm not sure. A fat fellow.
[END OF TAPE VI-A, SIDE 2]
You believe he was a former member of Jimmy Lunceford's band.
Jimmy Lunceford's band. He was a trumpet
Holmes (12/5) - 48
player. Now, what am I doing? Naming the personnel in there?
Yeah, if possible, of the...
You were asking who was the trumpet player.
Yeah. You had Sleepy, Moses Garland...
Moses Garland on trumpet and...
Clyde Bernhardt on trombone.
...Clyde Bernhardt on trombone.
You on alto.
Me on alto. Joe himself... And he would always hire a third alto. You know, it was nobody steady. He was using Les Carr for a while. And different ones, different ones he hired.
Did he use a steady drummer?

No, not at that time, because... Well, he was using a steady drummer at that time, but he was kind of tied up with his car... He had a station wagon, and he used to do a lot of moving people, running them down to the beaches and one-thing-or-another. So he wasn't always available. It wasn't convenient for him to make all of the jobs, because he might be out for a week or so with a group of people, and this-that-and-the-other.
So Joe was experimenting with different drummers for different engagements, this-that-and-the-other, until I told
Holmes (12/5) - 49

him about Rick, a guy named Harewood(?). And he tried Rick, and that made him. He was crazy about Rick. So that was good, because Rick was a very steady drummer. The only thing was he would make Joe mad, because if he promised to work with somebody else on a gig before Joe would hand him his list of gigs... Joe thought he should send somebody else on these other gigs. But Rick wasn't that way. If he told you he was going to work for you, he was going to work for you. You know, certain nights, one of them things. Well, they were always working(?) on him about that. But other than that... Yeah, Rick was still one of the band. I mean, if the band had still been going, he would still be there.
